header: Stereo. H C J D A 38
body: W.P.No.738/2023 Mst. Maryam Zafar VS. Additional Sessions Judge, Muzaffargarh etc.

Ch. Muhammad Iqbal, J:- Brief facts of the case are that Mst. Maryam Zafar, petitioner/plaintiff filed a suit for dissolution of marriage, recovery of dower, maintenance allowance and dowry articles against her huband- Muhammad Usman Ghani-the respondent No.3/defendant with the contentions that marriage of the petitioner/plaintiff was solemnized with her real maternal cousin/ respondent No.3 on 28.12.2016 and the dower was settled as Rs.5000/- cash, 2-1/2 tola gold ornaments, one Bigah land in Moza Rampur, 02 Marla house situated in Riaz-ul-Jannah Society and 02 Marla house situated in Mohalla Dosaywala. That the parents of the petitioner/plaintiff gave dowry articles, the detail whereof is mentioned in paragraph No.2 of the plaint. That the petitioner/plaintiff started performing her matrimonial obligations but despite spousal relationship of two years, no issue was born from the said wedlock. That the petitioner/plaintiff and respondent No.3/defendant voluntarily got themselves medically examined and the respondent No.3/defendant was diagnosed infertility. That on 20.04.2020, when petitioner/plaintiff asked for Date of hearing 22.10.2026 Petitioner by Malik Riaz Ahmad Khakhi, Advocate Respondent No.3 by Muhammad Shafi Mirali, Advocate W.P.No.738/2023 2 payment of maintenance allowance and transfer the properties as mentioned in Nikahnama, the respondent No.3/defendant kicked out the petitioner/plaintiff from his house and thereafter made no bonafide effort for rehabilitation of spousal bounds which culminated into filing of the suit.

The respondent No.3/defendant filed contesting written statement and controverted the contents of the plaint on legal and factual grounds. Besides above defensive assertions he also filed a suit for jactitation of marriage. The trial court [learned Judge Family Court, Muzaffargarh] consolidated both the suits, framed issues, recorded evidence and vide consolidated judgment & decree dated 24.09.2022, partly decreed the suit of the petitioner/plaintiff whereas dismissed the suit for jactitation of marriage filed by respondent No.3/defendant in the following manner:

“13. For what has been discussed above, the suit of the plaintiff for dissolution of marriage is hereby decreed on the basis of khula is decreed against the defendant subject to relinquishment of dower, and the suit of the plaintiff for recovery of maintenance allowance is partially decreed in the manner that she is entitled for maintenance allowance @ Rs.5000/- per month during the period of iddat, suit of the plaintiff for recovery of dower is hereby dismissed. The suit of plaintiff for recovery of dowry articles is hereby partially decreed in the manner that she is entitled to receive alternate price of dowry articles Rs.1,50,000/-. The suit of the defendant for jactitation of marriage is hereby dismissed being frivolous and defendant shall pay Rs.500,000/- as damages to the plaintiff for false prosecution.”

Being disgruntled from the above determinations/dictum both the parties filed separate appeals and the appellate Court [learned Addl. District Judge, Muzaffargarh] vide consolidated judgment & decree dated 28.11.2022, decided the appeals in the following manner:

“20. For what has been discussed above, findings of learned Trial Court to the extent of issue No.01, 02 & issue No.06 are modified and cost Rs.200,000/- is imposed upon respondent for false prosecution instead of Rs.500,000/-, similarly, appellant/plaintiff is held entitled to recover dowry articles as W.P.No.738/2023 3 mentioned in Para No.02 of her plaint excluding items No.xxv, xxxvi, xxxvii, xxxxii and xxxxiii or alternate value of these articles i.e. Rs.400,000. Whereas, to the extent of remaining claims of parties, findings of learned Trial Court are up-held.” Hence, this petition.

2. The respondent No.3/defendant challenged the judgments & decrees through Writ Petition [No.19368/2022] but he has withdrawn the said writ petition today vide order of even date as such to his extent, the judgments & decrees of the Courts below have attained status of finality.
3. Arguments heard. Record perused.
4. Issues No.3 & 5 relate to the dissolution of marriage and recovery of maintenance allowance, which are reproduced as under:

“3. Whether the plaintiff is entitled to decree for dissolution of marriage on the basis of Khula? If so then to what effect? OPP 5. Whether the plaintiff is entitled to recover dower or its alternate value from the defendant as prayed for? OPP” The petitioner/plaintiff in paragraph No.4 of her plaint has categorically stated that in the medical checkup, the respondent No.3 was found deficient of fertility. For ready reference, paragraph No.4 of the plaint is reproduced as under: "4.ہیدمہیعدماع ہکوک دعبدمہیع اسل دو رکیتریہ۔ رکوقحقزوتیجادا وہ رتصخ رھگ ےک ہیلع دای رقار ٹف دمہیع وک وت رکاای اپ کیچ ےن دمہیع ۔ ے ئدی رک رشوع دےنی ےنعط ےک وہےن ہن اوالد کیچ ذموکرہ اک ہیلع دماع رھپ ایگ۔وہا۔ اثتب صقن اک رکےن دیپا اوالد ںیم ہیلع دماع وت ایگ رکاای اپ دمٹف رپاَن وطر ڈیمیلکی یھبدماعہیلع ےکابووجد اکاہکاس یھبدماعہیلعوکالعجرکاےن ہیعےنرھپ راہ۔"

The petitioner/plaintiff while submitting her affidavit in the shape of statement-in-chief stated in this regard as under: "4.ہک وہں رکیت حلفاایبنحلفہ م دو ریہ۔ رکیت ادا زوتیج وقحق رک وہ رتصخ رھگ ےک ہیلع دماع اسلدعبحلفہ م ۔ ے ئدےنیرشوعرکدی ےکےنعط وکاوالدہنوہےنحلفہ م ےنکیچاپرکاایوتحلفہ م وکٹف کیچ رھپدماعہیلعاکذموکرہ رقاردایایگ۔اثتب رکےناکصقن دیپا اپرکاایایگوتدماعہیلعںیماوالد W.P.No.738/2023 4 وہا۔حلفہ م اَن رپ وطر ڈیمیلکی ہیلع دماع یھب ابووجد ےک اس اہک اک رکاےن وکالعج ہیلع دماع یھب رھپ ےن ٹفراہ۔"

While appearing as P.W.1, the petitioner/plaintiff on oath repeated the same facts as mentioned in paragraph No.4 of the plaint and during cross examination, she also corroborated this stance by deposing that:

"ےکروزیلہپراتےھجمملعوہایگاھت۔ اشدیےسےلہپدماعہیلعیکانرمدییکابتبملعہناھت۔اشدی وادلہ وک یک ہیلع دماع ےن ںیم وجاجےئ وہ کیھٹ اور العج اقلب امیبری ہی ہک اہک ےن وہنجں اھت۔ اتبای اگ۔۔۔دماعہیلعیکوادلہیکیلستےکدعبیھبدماعہیلعیکوقترمدیاحبلہنوہیکس۔" The petitioner/plaintiff produced the report of medical test of the respondent No.3 as Mark-G. Zafar Iqbal (P.W.2) supported the stance of the petitioner/plaintiff.
Conversely, Muhammad Usman Ghani (D.W.1) denied his marriage with the petitioner/plaintiff.

5. The petitioner/plaintiff claimed in her suit that due to cruel behaviour of the respondent No.3/defendant, she cannot continue the spousal relationship. The term “cruelty” has been defined in Section 2 of the Dissolution of Muslim Marriages Act, 1939 as under:

“2. Grounds for decree for dissolution of marriage. A woman married under Muslim Law shall be entitled to obtain a decree for the dissolution of her marriage on any one or more of the following grounds, namely:-- (viii) that the husband treats her with cruelty, that is to say: (a) habitually assaults her or makes her life miserable by cruelty of conduct, even if such conduct does not amount to physical ill-treatment; or (b) associates with women of evil repute or leads an infamous life; or (c) attempts to force her to lead an immoral life; or (d) disposes of her property or prevents her from exercising her legal rights over it; or (e) obstructs her in the observance of her religious profession or practice; or W.P.No.738/2023 5 (f) if he has more wives than one, does not treat her equitably in accordance with the injunctions of the Quran.”

[emphasis supplied] The Hon'ble Supreme Court of Pakistan in Dr. Seema Hanif Khan’s case has held that the “cruelty” is not limited only to physical harm rather it includes any conduct which results in mental and emotional harm and has held as under:

“6. We take up the ground of cruelty first. The legislature did not attempt to define cruelty in the DMMA; instead, it provided a series of illustrations that show the range of conduct that can fall within this ground. These illustrations show that cruelty can range from physical assault, to mental or emotional abuse, to interference with property or religion, to inequitable treatment in the context of a second marriage. The examples listed in Section 2 (viii) of the DMMA are not exhaustive but illustrative, ensuring that courts remain flexible in recognizing cruelty in its many different forms. Accordingly, cruelty is not limited to physical harm rather it includes any conduct, which results in mental and emotional harm, that makes it impossible for the wife to live with dignity and security within the marital home and relationship.

7. As per our jurisprudence, courts have defined cruelty as being behavior which is not limited to physical abuse but involves behavior which can result in mental and emotional abuse. Therefore, cruelty encompasses physical harm; such as slaps, beatings or assault, as well as mental cruelty, such as humiliation, verbal abuse, or unfounded allegations of unfaithfulness in a marriage; emotional cruelty, such as neglect or indifference; and, at times, the broader environment of the marriage, such as hostility in the home or oppressive behavior by in-laws tolerated or encouraged by the husband. It is also held that cruelty can involve a series of acts, disconnected but collectively causing harm which renders it intolerable for the wife to remain in the marriage bond. Courts have also expanded on what constitutes cruelty by holding that cruelty includes the intentional or malicious infliction of mental suffering, abusive treatment, or false accusations. This means that physical injury is not a prerequisite and cruelty may consist entirely of conduct that causes anguish, loss of confidence, or injury to selfrespect and may even encompass violent or non-violent acts, gestures, words, and even silence or neglect. More recently this Court has held that cruelty may be physical or mental, intentional or unintentional, premeditated or not. Essentially, it is behavior, the impact of which is so painful, so severe, and so harsh that it would be impossible to live in the marriage. This Court emphasized that the conduct and the impact of that conduct is relevant because marriage is seen as a bond where there is trust, respect, love and affection failing which, where a woman seeks dissolution of marriage, a court must examine whether that conduct was so unbearable that she no longer wishes to maintain the marital bond. In this way, we note that, as per the jurisprudence, the relevant and decisive factor is the impact of the husband’s conduct on the woman Dr. Seema Hanif Khan Vs. Waqas Khan and others (PLD 2026 SC 91)

W.P.No.738/2023 6 such that she no longer deems it possible to live with him. Accordingly, for a court examining whether a case of cruelty is made out to dissolve the marriage, cruelty must be assessed in all its forms in the context of its impact whether physical, mental, emotional, and even environmental.

9. Cruelty under the DMMA is related to the conduct of the husband such that his behavior or treatment towards the wife involves physical abuse in the form of assault as well as emotional and mental abuse such that his conduct is so reprehensive for her that she is miserable and unable to live with him. This means that cruelty can be physical, mental as well as emotional. It involves an element of abuse, whether physical or verbal, or through behavior or conduct which in the mind of the married woman is harmful, unsafe and impossible to live with. More importantly, it does not have to be a continuous form of behavior but can be a pattern of behavior that undermines her dignity, lifestyle, peace of mind and health. So, the question of cruelty is sensitive to social contexts, personalities, and lived realities of marriage. Accordingly, cruelty in matrimonial cases is not to be judged by a standard so rigid that it replicates a criminal trial. The question is not whether guilt has been established beyond reasonable doubt, but whether the conduct complained of, viewed in the context of the marriage, is such that the wife cannot reasonably be expected to continue with the relationship. Cruelty is therefore a subjective test, to be assessed in light of the effect of the behavior on the aggrieved woman, rather than by reference to strict categories or technical rules of proof.”
In Mst. Tayyeba Ambareen’s case, the Hon'ble Supreme Court of Pakistan held that:

“9. The cruelty alleged may be mental or physical, premeditated or unpremeditated, but lack of intent does not make any distinction. Obviously, if it is a physical act then it would be a question of fact, and in the event of mental cruelty, an enquiry is required to be made as to the nature of the cruel treatment to find out the impact or repercussions thereof on the mind of the spouse. Mental cruelty can be largely delineated as a course of conduct which perpetrates mental pain with such a severity and harshness which would render it impossible for that party to continue the matrimonial tie or to live together. The matrimonial relationship is based on a mutual trust between wife and husband with emotions and it obliges reciprocal respect, love and affection for evenhanded adjustments with the spouse without causing a sense of anguish and disappointment, therefore, while deciding any lis for dissolution of marriage on the ground of cruelty, the Court must adjudge the intensity and ruthlessness of the acts and examine whether the conduct complained of is not merely a trivial issue which may happen in day-to-day married life, but is of such a nature which no reasonable person can endure.”

The petitioner/plaintiff has proved that the respondent No.3 conducted physical and mental torture upon her. The suit for Mst. Tayyeba Ambareen and another Vs. Shafqat Ali Kiyani and another (2023 SCMR 246) W.P.No.738/2023 7 jactitation of marriage filed by the respondent No.3/defendant strengthens the stance of the petitioner/plaintiff as the petitioner/plaintiff lived for more than two years with the respondent No.3/defendant, even despite issue of fertility of the respondent No.3, and when she asked for dissolution of marriage and payment of dower, the respondent No.3 came up with suit for jactitation of marriage.

While deciding the issues No.3 & 5, the Courts below did not discuss the pleadings/plaint, statement-in-chief of petitioner (Exh.P.1), cross examination conducted upon the statement of P.W.1 and also did not discuss the medical report (Mark-G) of the respondent No.3/defendant.

6. Moreover, the respondent No.3/defendant has denied his Nikah with the petitioner in his written statement and also filed a suit for jactitation of marriage whereas the petitioner proved the solemnization of marriage with the respondent No.3/defendant through oral as well documentary evidence and the Courts below concurrently decided this issue in favour of the petitioner/plaintiff. Today, learned counsel for the respondent No.3/defendant has withdrawn the Writ Petition [No.19368/2022] filed by the respondent No.3 against the dismissal of his suit for jactitation of marriage as well as appeal by the Courts below. Through the suit for jactitation of marriage, the respondent No.3/defendant tried to scandalize the reputation of the petitioner/plaintiff which proves that the respondent No.3/defendant is not a truthful witness.

7. Further, in paragraph No.6 of the plaint, the petitioner/plaintiff has asserted that due to the torturous conduct of the respondent No.3/defendant, an acute hatred has been developed against him and her marriage may be dissolved on this ground. For ready reference, paragraph No.6 of the plaint is reproduced as under:
W.P.No.738/2023 8 "ہیہکدمہیعوکدماعہیلعےسدشدیرفنتےہ۔امنیبرفنیقیاھبنہادنردحوداہللاننکممےہ۔دمہیع دماعہیلعےکرھگآابدوہےنےسومتوکرتحیجدیتیےہ۔دمہیعاکدوعیٰ ذینہرپاشییناوردشتدیکانبء رپڈرگیرفامایاجےئ۔"

8. The petitioner/plaintiff claimed the dissolution of marriage on the basis of mental teasing and physical torture conducted by the respondent No.3 and she proved the same through corroborative evidence as such she is entitled for grant of her claim for dissolution of marriage on such basis but the Courts below have ignored the above domestic compulsive and coercive circumstances and illegally and unlawfully dissolved the marriage on the basis of Khula as such the findings of the Courts below on Issues No.3 & 5 are unsustainable and same are hereby reversed and aforesaid issues are decided in favour of the petitioner/plaintiff in the manner that the marriage between the petitioner and respondent No.3 is dissolved on the basis of mental and physical cruelty inflicted upon her by the respondent No.3 and the petitioner/plaintiff is held entitled to recover dower as mentioned in her Nikah-Nama as per law whereas the rest of the findings of the Courts below are maintained.

9. Resultantly, this Writ Petition is partly allowed only to the extent of issues No.3 & 5 as discussed above and the judgments & decrees of the Courts below are modified accordingly. The petitioner is also entitled for special cost of rupees five lac to be recovered from the respondent No.3/defendant as money decree in favour of the petitioner/plaintiff for the reason that the petitioner/plaintiff has suffered physical and mental cruelty not only during the period she lived with the respondent No.3 but also thereafter in the shape of denial of the respondent No.3 regarding his marriage with the plaintiff and filing of suit for jactitation of marriage by respondent No.3 against the petitioner, as well as that, the petitioner/plaintiff has been waiting to receive her W.P.No.738/2023 9 legal claim since 2020 after filing suit for dissolution of marriage and recovery of dower and dowry articles.
(Ch. Muhammad Iqbal)
